risks.title: Fluctuations in yen/dollar foreign exchange rates
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned prominently in the Risk Factors section and detailed extensively in Item 7A. The company is significantly exposed through its Japan operations and substantial yen-denominated investments. Exchange rate fluctuations directly impact the translation of yen-denominated assets/liabilities into USD for reporting, and the company notes potential for significant cash strain at the parent company level from derivative settlements and collateral requirements.

risks.title: Interest rate risk on fixed income investments
risks.score_rationale: Interest rate risk is identified as a primary market risk factor affecting the company's investment portfolio. The company holds a significant portion of fixed maturity securities which are sensitive to rate changes. Item 7A explicitly identifies this as one of the primary market risks monitored regularly.

risks.title: Credit risk on fixed income securities
risks.score_rationale: The document indicates that a significant portion of the investment portfolio is composed of fixed maturity securities, exposing the company to counterparty credit risk. The company monitors credit risk through various strategies, suggesting material exposure.

risks.title: Geographic concentration of investments in Japan
risks.score_rationale: The company's Japan segment generates the vast majority of earnings and the investment portfolio shows significant concentration in yen-denominated securities. The MD&A indicates that Aflac Japan's functional currency is the yen and a material portion of the portfolio supports yen-denominated liabilities, creating concentration risk.

risks.title: Derivative and hedging program risks
risks.score_rationale: Item 7A details extensive use of foreign currency forwards, options, and other derivatives for hedging purposes. The company acknowledges rollover risk, basis risk, and the potential for significant derivative losses during periods of yen movement. The company notes explicit risks from shorter-duration derivatives hedging longer-duration investments.

risks.title: Liquidity strain from foreign exchange derivatives settlement
risks.score_rationale: Item 7A explicitly states that if yen strengthens significantly, this could cause cash strain at the parent company from derivative cash settlements and collateral requirements, and notes this could be significant depending on timing and severity of rate movements. The company manages this through ongoing hedging program adjustments.
